pairs.why: The two cups are almost the same, but A's small bubbles on the tea match the real juice glass's liquid detail better than B's flat, glossy surface.
This is the mirror of q000: B has the bubbled tea surface, which reads more like the real liquid rendering than A's plain glassy tea.
A's soft, slightly matte charcoal felt matches the soft finish of the real jacket, while B's purple sheen leans toward the glossy statue look that lessons 1 and 2 rejected.
This is the mirror of q002: B has the softer matte felt, and A's purple-tinted gloss looks more like a plastic statue.
A's eyelet lace on the ruffle is a built-in detail, like the tooled saddle the art lead preferred, and the rest of A stays as smooth and chunky as the real cards.
This is the mirror of q004: B has the lace-trimmed ruffle, which makes the object better built without making the surface texture-y.
A has a bright, saturated background like the real cards and a properly built knurled winding crown, while B is darker and duller, with a plain knob.
This is the mirror of q006: B has the bright, saturated green and the knurled crown, while A's dark green and plain knob don't match the vivid real cards.
